newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end narrowly mixed.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended narrowly mixed, as June T-bonds held on to gains due to technically driven short-covering.

June bonds rallied into -- and after -- U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's prepared testimony to a House Banking subcommittee was unchanged from the first leg of his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony last week.
Traders attributed the late gains to a technical short-covering rally after June bonds failed to find sellers below 109-19/32.
"We just had no followthrough," one trader said.
June T-bonds probed below the 200-day moving average of 109-21/32 after Greenspan's testimony was released.

However, locals covered short positions and dealers turned into bidders when the decline stalled at 109-19/32. Earlier in the day, the contract also limited losses at 109-19/32, above the daily low of 109-17/32.

June T-bonds rose to 110-05/32 on the best volume of the day, traders said. They estimated total bond futures volume at 375,000 contracts, and pegged near-term resistance at 110-08/32. Some said the contract could test that level since it managed to close above 109-21/32 to 109-22/32 area.
Eurodollar futures also rose in tandem with T-bonds, but most ended the day unchanged.

Wednesday marks the thirteenth session in a row in which September and June have closed lower or unchanged. June and September, however, still remain above their 200-day moving averages at 93.98 and 93.84, respectively.
Analysts said both bonds and Eurodollars were both oversold from last week's selloff. While neither market has triggered a buy signal, they said both markets were prone to light short-covering.

At the end of pit trade, June T-bonds were up 04/32 at 109-30/32, 10-year notes were up 02/32 at 107-14/32, muni bonds were up 08/32 at 114-02/32, June T-bills were up 0.015 basis point at 94.75, June Eurodollars were unchanged at 94.18 and September Eurodollars were down 0.005 at 93.975.
